find: if (key === null) return { patched: text, count: 0 };
replace: if (key === null) return patchField(text, field, value);
why: Falls back to a GLOBAL patch when the profile id does not match -- the natural wrong implementation, and the worst possible one here. A typo in --profile would then sweep all eight profiles together while the run's own header said "profile X only", so the report would describe a personality difference that was actually a global rebalance. The caller refuses on count 0, which is why returning 0 rather than guessing is the whole contract.
killedBy: patchProfileField: one profile, and only that one REFUSES an unknown profile rather than patching everything
